scope: NtQueryInformationFile class 18 / FileAllInformation for named synchronous CreateFileA/W regular files and directories, plus NtQueryVolumeInformationFile class 1 / FileFsVolumeInformation for the mounted virtual C: profile.
behavior: CreateFile resolves host and canonical guest paths from one process-CWD snapshot. Its immutable native open record retains the volume-relative ASCII guest name, expanded Win32 access mask and synchronous/sequential mode. Same-access duplicates retain the record; borrowed descriptors and metadata are copied together under the handle registry lock.

File metadata comes from the owned fstat descriptor: birth/access/write/change times converted to 1601-based 100ns units, readonly/hidden/directory/archive attributes, allocated blocks, EOF, link count and inode. Position is the actual current shared file offset, read without moving it. Directories have zero logical/allocated content size. Windows EAs, delete-on-close and unbuffered alignment are not exposed by this profile.

FileAllInformation uses independently compiled i686 MSVC field offsets. The full filename byte length is at offset96 and non-terminated UTF16 characters at100. At length104 the caller normally receives STATUS_BUFFER_OVERFLOW with IOSB Information104 and the first two characters. Odd excess bytes stay untouched; full buffers return success and the actual written length.

The virtual C: volume label is TribesPad, not the native host volume label. Its serial is the backing mount f_fsid.val[0], stable for that mount session, not a persistent physical disk ID. Unsupported Windows volume creation time and object-ID support are zero. The variable label starts at18; a24-byte query yields overflow with the first three characters. Existing class4 device semantics remain.
Both output ranges are preflighted and their permission epoch retained until the record and x86 IOSB are copied. Native syscalls only receive host-owned buffers. CPU/stdcall/LastError are preserved.

Unsupported classes/objects still stop. Invalid/short/misaligned output preconditions or handles leave buffers unchanged. Bare adopted descriptors have no invented path/open-mode record and return STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED. A renamed/replaced/unlinked host pathname is detected by lstat identity and also returns STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED.
validation: Mac normal/ThreadSanitizer/checked and sole guarded iPad, actual regular file/directory descriptors, metadata-only and generic read/write access, duplicated handle metadata and close lifetime, file offset, hard links, readonly changes, later CWD changes, filename truncation/capacity matrix and volume label/serial.

Seven guarded failures (file and volume record/status/cross-page writes and unsupported class); Mac shared-memory fork checks prove no partial output on rejected accesses. Short/invalid/type/closed/raw handle cases and sentinel tails are checked.

Independent i686-pc-windows-msvc compilation verifies Microsoft WDK structure sizes/offsets without Apple native packing assumptions. Real dynamic ntdll lookup resolves and executes the new wrapper;90 finite provider exports remain disjoint.
limits: No direct native Windows comparison was available. Structure layout is checked for the guest ABI; four-byte user-buffer alignment and precondition ordering follow the existing NT bridge profile, rather than a captured Windows class18 experiment.

The guest filesystem supports ASCII existing paths, buffered synchronous opens, and no Windows extended attributes, token/DACL or delete-pending model. Final symbolic-link-object FileAllInformation remains unsupported; followed paths retain their resolved open name. Host rename/unlink equivalence is not implemented.

Volume identity is explicitly virtual and mount-session based; no persistent serial, actual native volume birth date, physical-media identity, NTFS features, network/read-only mount execution or asynchronous completion is claimed.

Queries are snapshots of individual native attributes, not an atomic snapshot against concurrent external host file changes. Unexpected native inspection/position failures return STATUS_UNSUCCESSFUL without an IOSB completion.
No game window, rendered map, HD, gameplay controls, physical-device execution or authenticated match acceptance follows from these component tests.
